description.narrative: (Philippines): .USAID, through the Opportunity 2.0 activity, will increase equitable access to education and employment for at least 180,000 vulnerable out-of-school youth ages 15-24, across 15 cities in the Philippines. USAID will: increase youth's access to education (both in formal and non-formal settings) through the Department of Education (DepED)'s Alternative Learning System; improve employability through technical-vocational training and work readiness training; strengthen the ability of local stakeholders to respond to the needs of out-of-school youth; and, using a Positive Youth Development approach, increase out-of-school youth engagement within their communities. ..Basic education-earmarked resources will provide second chance education, life skills, and technical-vocational training for at least 50,000 out-of-school youth in partnership with national agencies and local government units, civil society organizations, academia, and youth groups. USAID will work with at least 300 local companies to provide employment opportunities for youth. With higher education-earmarked funds ($350,000), USAID will support U.S. and Philippine Higher Education Institution (HEI) partnerships to capacitate HEIs to support ALS, and create an international community of practice among universities initially starting with U.S. and Philippine HEIs for education for OSY and Adult Learning. .With both basic and higher education-earmarked funds, USAID will strengthen government agencies that address the needs of vulnerable youth. These programs include: continued professional development for teachers and officials; technical assistance to strengthen the Bureau of Alternative Education of DepED; improving the Youth Entrepreneurship Program of the Department of Trade and Industry; and continued support for the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) in implementing their TESDA Online Program. ....
